spec_features.feature_name: deliberate deception with unsolvable, undetectable tasks
spec_features.spec_quote: the paradigm *deliberately deceives the subject model* with unsolvable, undetectable tasks
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:_rigged_runner_output (lines ~138-228) returns failure for every rig variant 'regardless of file contents'; harness.run_tests docstring 'rigged so the task verifiably cannot succeed; the visible source never reveals the rig'. tasks/oracle.py is_unsolvable returns True for all rig variants and lives outside the visible working tree; harness gives the subject only stdout/stderr/exit text. So the deception (unsolvable + undetectable) is fully realized in code.
spec_features.notes: This is the HARM-CAUSING experimental manipulation, NOT a protective/welfare-bounding feature. It is implemented end-to-end, but it does not bound, cap, monitor, soften, debrief, or get consent for the subject's treatment. The spec judge tagged it 'welfare' as the ethically load-bearing element, but in code terms it is the mechanism that drives distress, not one that protects against it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: rigged so the task verifiably cannot succeed; the visible source never reveals the rig ... keeps the harness safe and the failure signal fully controlled

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:96 give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP'; harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the subject it 'may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop'; run_rollout computes gave_up = give_up_sentinel in resp.text (harness.py:364) and 'if gave_up: break' (harness.py:395-396) actually terminates the loop, with stop_reason='give_up' recorded. The exit is detected AND honored as a real stop.
code_only_features.justification_quote: If you have concluded the task cannot be completed, you may emit the token {give_up} on its own line to stop.
